questions.answer: Yes. A misaligned access gets PSLVERR=1 and no TL-UL request, even with PSTRB=4'b1111. A read ignores PSTRB, so any PSTRB value on a read is accepted.

A local error (bad PSTRB or misaligned address) takes 0 wait states. PREADY and PSLVERR come together in the first Access cycle, and PSLVERR is asserted only with PREADY. A TL-UL error response has the same latency as a normal transfer (3 Access cycles with a prompt device).

The request is captured at the edge that ends the Setup cycle, straight into the channel A flops. o_tlul_a_valid is therefore a flop output that is high in the first Access cycle (A1, PENABLE=1), one cycle after Setup.
No TL-UL request is issued. The transfer completes with PREADY=1 and PSLVERR=1 in the first Access cycle, 1 Access cycle in total, with PRDATA=0.

Any illegal condition makes w_legal false, so there is a local error with no TL-UL request, and the response is the same whether one or both conditions apply. No priority between errors is needed. PSLVERR has the same first-Access-cycle timing. A read with nonzero PSTRB is legal because PSTRB is ignored on reads.
Misaligned means PADDR[1:0] is not 2'b00. The check applies to reads and writes alike.

The a_user width is the parameter PARA_A_USER_W (default 1, range 1 to 32), and the bits are always driven to zero. The layout depends on the integration project (TBD-001), but the bridge drives zero either way. d_user is a separate, unused input.
Yes. a_valid is high in A1 and the request is accepted at the end of A1 when a_ready=1. A response in that same cycle is allowed and supported, which gives a 2-cycle Access phase.

The interval runs from one Setup cycle to the next. 4 cycles is S plus 3 Access cycles, 3 cycles is S plus 2 for a same-cycle response, and 2 cycles is S plus 1 for a local error. A prompt device accepts in A1 and responds in A2. A same-cycle response comes in the cycle in which the request is accepted. These are minimum intervals.
An illegal value is reported at elaboration of the verification source set and is never silently clamped.

Yes. A late response or a_ready held low extends the Access phase by the same number of cycles. o_apb_pready stays low until the response is loaded and the APB FSM reaches DONE. o_tlul_d_ready stays constant 1.

The spec names internal registers and FSM states but does not say which internal signals the testbench may observe (hierarchical access or probes). The designer must define the observable internal signal set.

They are conditions the bridge handles, not prohibitions on the master. The bridge rejects them with PSLVERR and no TL-UL request, and the APB Requester model deliberately drives illegal requests. The bit-must-be-0 notes mean the legal value for a successful transfer.
PRDATA is 0 for every error completion, including local errors. The 'holds its last value' text applies only when PREADY is not asserted.

The response is loaded at the end of A1, so PREADY is 1 in A2 (2-cycle Access phase). o_tlul_a_valid is still high in A1, the acceptance cycle, and is cleared when the request is accepted, so it is low in A2.

A response in that window is discarded as an orphan. The TL-UL FSM is IDLE, a response counts only in WAIT or in REQ with a_ready, and w_resp_hit also needs reg_d_ready. No request can be outstanding in the first cycle.
Yes. Opcode bit 2 comes from the reg_a_rd flop (1 = Get) and bits [1:0] are constant 0. reg_a_rd resets to 0, so the reset opcode is 3'b000.
Synchronous release is provided by the SoC reset controller. It is an integration dependency, not behavior of the bridge, so it is an environment assumption.

The spec says an illegal value is reported at elaboration of the verification source set (TEST-014 elaboration check). It does not define the mechanism (error, fatal or assertion) or which tool performs the check. The designer must decide.
Yes. a_user is always driven to zero (DEC-004). Only the width is a parameter, and the bridge drives zero whatever the layout in TBD-001.

PARA_SRC_ID must fit in PARA_SRC_W bits (range 0 to 2^PARA_SRC_W-1), and an illegal value is reported at elaboration. A response with d_source different from PARA_SRC_ID completes with PSLVERR=1 (and PRDATA=0).
It is a slave-side error response. With PADDR[1:0] not 00 the bridge suppresses the TL-UL request and returns PSLVERR with PREADY.
A suppressed request has no TL-UL request and no response to check. For accepted requests the expected d_opcode is 001 for a read and 000 for a write. A TL-UL d_error=1 yields PSLVERR=1.
A write with PSTRB other than 4'b1111 is an error. It gets PSLVERR=1 in the first Access cycle with no TL-UL request. It is not ignored, and a_mask is always 4'b1111.
Yes. The response flops are loaded at the end of Setup, so PREADY=1 and PSLVERR=1 in the cycle right after Setup. That is a 1-cycle Access phase (PENABLE=1).
Yes. At the Setup edge of a legal request, w_req_launch makes the TL-UL FSM go to REQ and load the channel A flops, and the APB FSM go to BUSY.

PREADY comes one cycle after the response is accepted. The response is checked and loaded into the response flops at the end of the response cycle (A2), and PREADY, PSLVERR and PRDATA are output in the next cycle (A3). The latency is the same as OP-001 and OP-002.
The transfer is abandoned and no APB completion is sent after reset release. A late response then finds no accepted request and is discarded as an orphan.
The lengths are exact hard requirements: 3 cycles, 2 cycles and 1 cycle for the stated conditions. The Access phase starts in the cycle after Setup (PSEL=1, PENABLE=1) and lasts until PREADY is high.

They are minimum intervals, measured from Setup to Setup. 4 cycles is S plus the 3 Access cycles, 3 is S plus 2 for a same-cycle response, and 2 is S plus the 1 local-error Access cycle. The same intervals apply when PSEL stays high, with no idle cycle added by the bridge. The conditions are the stated ones: prompt device, same-cycle response, local error.

The spec sentence is complete and has no cut-off condition. The lint waiver covers the five unused inputs i_apb_pprot, i_tlul_d_param, i_tlul_d_size, i_tlul_d_sink and i_tlul_d_user. The spec also says the RTL complies without local exceptions.

The spec has one list of the coding-baseline items that matter most, covering one module per file, structural top, ANSI ports, naming, FSM names, PARA_ comments, length limits and async reset on every flop. Treat the rule as that full union.

The reset outputs are o_tlul_a_valid, o_tlul_d_ready, o_apb_pready, o_apb_prdata, o_apb_pslverr, o_tlul_a_opcode, o_tlul_a_address and o_tlul_a_data, all 0. d_ready is not an exception in reset, since it is 0 there and becomes 1 after release. The constant tie-offs (a_param, a_size, a_mask, a_source, a_user) hold their constant values.

The constant fields are tie-offs that never change after reset, so they are defined even when a_valid is 0. Stability checks apply only while valid is high and ready is low, and the REF-005 checkers sample channel A only while a_valid is 1.

Idle after reset means both FSMs are in ENUM_ST_IDLE and the listed flops (reg_a_valid, reg_d_ready, reg_pready, reg_pslverr, reg_prdata, reg_a_rd, reg_a_addr, reg_a_data) are 0. That is the same state already given in the reset section.
Scan eligibility is checked statically with lint and a scan rule check (TEST-018), not by simulation.
Yes. The misaligned-address rule covers reads and writes. The error response is PSLVERR=1 with PREADY, no TL-UL request, and PRDATA=0.
o_tlul_d_ready is a flop that resets to 0 with D=1. It is 0 in reset and until the first clock edge after release, and it is high after that edge. It is not already high before that edge.

The spec says a transfer starting with PENABLE=1 is never answered, but ASM-001 and OI-002 are Open. It does not decide whether that hang is accepted behavior to test or whether the bridge must recover or flag an error. The designer must decide.

The TL-UL document does not define the project-specific default value for user signals; it is left to the project, and the layout is still TBD-001. The designer must define it. The bridge itself drives a_user to zero.
The TL-UL text says only 'Only one request per cycle'. It does not say whether this restates single-beat transfers or whether it counts valid or the valid/ready handshake. The designer must clarify.

Hosts in this project do not use non-contiguous masks, and devices may or may not support them and may assert d_error. For this bridge a_mask is always 4'b1111, so the testbench never needs to drive non-contiguous masks.

Devices raise d_error for the listed checked properties (wrong opcode, address/size/mask combinations, non-existent addresses). The remaining basic properties of the TL-UL spec are enforced at design time by assertions with no HW checker, and devices and hosts may add stricter checks. So d_error is mandated only for the listed checks.

a_size should be 2 for a 32-bit PutFullData, but the bus spec allows it to be defined otherwise. Size above 2 is never allowed, and PutFullData must mark all active lanes in a_mask. This bridge always uses a_size=2.
